page.title: Digital Marketing Agency Workflow: Stages, Tools, and Handoffs
page.description: A step-by-step breakdown of the seven-stage workflow agencies use to move work from intake to reporting, with owners, tools, and approval gates.
page.h1: What does the digital marketing agency workflow look like?
page.definition: A digital marketing agency workflow is a repeatable sequence of stages that moves client work from intake through brief, production, review, approval, publishing, and reporting, with one owner and one output per stage.
page.quick_answer: Map your work into seven stages — intake, brief, production, review, approval, publishing, reporting — assign one owner per stage, and set an approval gate before each handoff.

sections.h2: What are the seven stages every agency workflow needs?

blocks.p: Seven stages, each with one owner and one output: intake, brief, production, review, approval, publishing, reporting.

ol: Intake — capture request, confirm scope, assign owner
Brief — write creative brief, align on KPIs, get sign-off
Review — internal quality check against brief
Approval — client sign-off on final assets
Publishing — deploy to agreed channels on schedule
Reporting — pull performance data, note learnings

sections.h2: Which tools support each stage without creating silos?

blocks.p: Common tools: Asana, Monday.com or Airtable for the calendar; Google Docs or Notion for briefs; WordPress, Webflow or HubSpot for publishing; GA4 and HubSpot for reporting.

sections.h2: How do you prevent work from stalling at review and approval?

blocks.p: Set a hard SLA for each gate, limit revision rounds, and require a named approver before the stage closes.

ul: Define maximum two revision rounds per deliverable
Assign a single decision-maker per client account
Automate reminders at 24 and 48 hours past due
Log every approval with timestamp and version link

sections.h2: What does a realistic timeline look like from brief to publish?

blocks.p: A realistic cycle for a long-form article is five to ten working days from approved brief to publish, most of it in review.

ul: Day one to two: production draft
Day four to five: client review and revisions
Day seven to eight: publishing and QA
Day nine to ten: reporting setup

sections.h2: How do you hand off work between team members without losing context?

blocks.p: Use a structured handoff template that travels with the task in your work management tool.

ul: Link to approved brief and brand assets
List open decisions and who owns them
Note version history and feedback summary
Confirm next stage owner and due date

sections.h2: When should you add AI assistance without breaking quality control?

blocks.p: Common tools: Asana, Monday.com or ClickUp for the workflow; ChatGPT or Claude for research and drafts; Adobe Firefly or Canva for image variants; Zapier or Make for hand-offs; HubSpot or GA4 for reporting.

ul: Research and outline generation in brief stage
First-draft copy and image variants in production
Automated status updates via Zapier or Make
Human-in-the-loop rule: AI output is a draft until a named person approves it

faq.q: How many stages should a small agency start with?
faq.a: Start with five stages — intake, brief, production, approval, publishing — and add review and reporting once the team can sustain the extra gates without slowing delivery.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to cut revision cycles?
faq.a: Require a signed brief with locked KPIs and reference examples before production begins, and cap client feedback to two consolidated rounds with a single point of contact.

faq.q: Which single metric best shows workflow health?
faq.a: Cycle time from approved brief to publish, broken down by stage, reveals bottlenecks better than utilisation or revision count alone.

faq.q: How do you onboard a freelancer into an existing workflow?
faq.a: Give them a sandbox project with the same templates, tool access, and approval gates; pair them with a staff producer for the first two deliveries before solo work.

faq.q: When is it worth building custom automation versus using native features?
faq.a: Build custom automation only when a handoff crosses three or more tools daily and the time saved exceeds the maintenance cost within one quarter.
